description: Tier 2 telemetry: metrics the application itself emits through library instrumentation (Micrometer, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus client libraries, client-library metrics such as a Kafka consumer's lag), organised by the same tech-stack modules as the Master NFR List. Everything here is tagged application level or library emitted. It is deliberately separate from the OneAgent default catalogue (tier 1). Stage 4's dashboard generator uses it as the second tier next to OneAgent defaults and business-aware custom metrics (tier 3), so an SRE sees for any service what OneAgent gives by default, what the application already emits, and what needs new instrumentation.
provenance: Curated from the libraries' own documentation (Micrometer, Spring Boot Actuator, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus client libraries, Apache Kafka, Resilience4j, HikariCP, Caffeine, Quarkus, Spring Cloud Gateway). Metric names are the library-native names; where a metric reaches Dynatrace through a registry or exporter the name may be transformed, so dashboards must be built from what the tenant actually receives. Entries with confidence medium depend on library version or optional configuration.
overlap_policy: Metrics in this catalogue and the OneAgent default catalogue must never be assumed to overlap or to be duplicates: OneAgent measures from outside the code with its own instrumentation, while these are emitted by the application. Where both measure something similar (for example request duration), the dashboard shows the OneAgent signal by default and offers the library metric as an additional, separately named series.

lang_java.summary: Libraries that emit metrics from any JVM application, independent of the framework.

libraries.configuration: Enabled by adding the SDK or attaching the OpenTelemetry Java agent; instrumentations are selected through OTEL_* environment variables or otel.* system properties.
libraries.export: OTLP exporter to a collector or to the observability platform's OTLP endpoint.

metrics.name: http.server.request.duration
metrics.description: Duration of inbound HTTP requests (semantic convention).

metrics.name: jvm.cpu.recent_utilization
metrics.description: Recent CPU utilisation of the JVM process.

libraries.configuration: A MetricRegistry with reporters (JMX, Graphite, Prometheus bridge) and the JVM metric sets registered explicitly.
libraries.export: Reporters such as JMX, Graphite, console or a Prometheus or Micrometer bridge.

libraries.configuration: DefaultExports.initialize() (simpleclient_hotspot) or the JVM metrics module registers the standard collectors; scraped from an HTTP endpoint.

metrics.name: process_cpu_seconds_total
metrics.description: CPU time consumed by the process.

libraries.configuration: Circuit breaker, retry, bulkhead, rate limiter and time limiter instances configured in code or resilience4j.* properties; metrics registered when a Micrometer or Prometheus binder is on the classpath.
libraries.export: Through Micrometer (resilience4j-micrometer) or the Prometheus module.

metrics.name: resilience4j.circuitbreaker.state
metrics.description: State of each circuit breaker (closed, open, half open).

metrics.name: resilience4j.circuitbreaker.calls
metrics.description: Calls by kind (successful, failed, ignored, not permitted).

metrics.name: resilience4j.circuitbreaker.failure.rate
metrics.description: Failure rate of the sliding window.

metrics.name: resilience4j.circuitbreaker.slow.call.rate
metrics.description: Share of calls slower than the slow-call threshold.

metrics.name: resilience4j.retry.calls
metrics.description: Calls by retry outcome (successful without retry, with retry, failed).

spring_boot.summary: Micrometer through Spring Boot Actuator, with auto-configured binders for the JVM, HTTP, data sources, caches and messaging.

libraries.configuration: Auto-configured by spring-boot-starter-actuator; meters are visible at /actuator/metrics once the metrics endpoint is exposed; management.metrics.* properties tune tags, distribution statistics and enabled binders.
libraries.export: A Micrometer registry on the classpath (Prometheus, OTLP, Dynatrace, others) or the actuator endpoint; without a registry the meters exist but leave the process nowhere.

metrics.name: jvm.memory.used
metrics.description: JVM memory used per area and pool.

metrics.name: jvm.memory.max
metrics.description: Maximum JVM memory per area and pool.

metrics.name: jvm.gc.memory.allocated
metrics.description: Memory allocated in young generation between collections.

metrics.name: process.cpu.usage
metrics.description: Recent CPU usage of the JVM process.

metrics.name: system.cpu.usage
metrics.description: Recent CPU usage of the whole system.

metrics.name: http.server.requests
metrics.description: Duration of inbound HTTP requests by method, uri, status and outcome.

metrics.name: http.client.requests
metrics.description: Duration of outbound HTTP requests made through Spring clients.

metrics.name: hikaricp.connections.usage
metrics.description: Time connections are held before being returned.

metrics.name: jdbc.connections.active
metrics.description: Active connections reported by the data source metadata.

metrics.name: spring.data.repository.invocations
metrics.description: Duration of Spring Data repository method calls.
metrics.note: Available in Spring Boot 3 with observation enabled for Spring Data.

metrics.name: cache.gets
metrics.note: Needs statistics enabled on the cache provider (for example recordStats for Caffeine).

metrics.name: executor.active
metrics.description: Active threads in each task executor.

metrics.name: executor.queued
metrics.description: Tasks queued for each task executor.

metrics.name: kafka.consumer.*
metrics.description: Kafka consumer client metrics bound by Micrometer (see the Kafka client library).

quarkus.summary: Micrometer or SmallRye Metrics through Quarkus extensions, with datasource and fault tolerance metrics.

libraries.configuration: Add quarkus-micrometer (with a registry extension) or quarkus-smallrye-metrics; quarkus.micrometer.* and quarkus.datasource.metrics.enabled control binders.
libraries.export: Prometheus endpoint at /q/metrics or another Micrometer registry extension.

metrics.name: agroal.awaiting.count
metrics.description: Threads waiting for a datasource connection.

lang_python.summary: Prometheus client and OpenTelemetry for Python services.

libraries.configuration: Default collectors register on import; start_http_server or an ASGI/WSGI exporter exposes them; multiprocess mode needs PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR.

metrics.name: process_cpu_seconds_total
metrics.description: CPU time consumed by the process.

metrics.name: python_gc_objects_collected_total
metrics.description: Objects collected by the garbage collector per generation.

libraries.configuration: opentelemetry-instrument or explicit SDK setup with instrumentation packages for the frameworks and clients in use.

metrics.name: http.server.duration
metrics.description: Duration of inbound HTTP requests (name depends on the semantic convention version).

metrics.name: db.client.operation.duration
metrics.description: Database client operation duration where a DB instrumentation is enabled.

lang_javascript_typescript.summary: prom-client and OpenTelemetry for Node.js services.

libraries.configuration: collectDefaultMetrics() must be called to register the default Node.js metrics.
libraries.export: Prometheus scrape endpoint served from the application.

libraries.configuration: The Node SDK with auto-instrumentations loaded before the application starts.

lang_go.summary: Prometheus client_golang and OpenTelemetry for Go services.

libraries.configuration: The default registry includes the Go and process collectors; promhttp.Handler() exposes them.

metrics.name: promhttp_metric_handler_requests_total
metrics.description: Scrapes of the metrics endpoint by status code.

libraries.configuration: SDK setup with instrumentation packages (otelhttp, otelsql) and the runtime instrumentation package.

metrics.name: go.goroutine.count
metrics.description: Goroutine count from the runtime instrumentation.

lang_rust.summary: Prometheus, metrics and OpenTelemetry crates. OneAgent has no Rust sensor, so these are the primary source of application telemetry.

libraries.configuration: Register collectors explicitly (no default process collector unless the process feature is enabled) and serve them over HTTP.

metrics.name: process_cpu_seconds_total
metrics.description: CPU time when the process feature is enabled.

libraries.configuration: Initialise the SDK and a tracing subscriber layer; instrument handlers with tracing spans.

metrics.name: http.server.request.duration
metrics.description: Only when instrumented through middleware such as tower-http or axum-tracing-opentelemetry.

libraries.configuration: RuntimeMonitor and TaskMonitor sampled in code.
libraries.export: Manually forwarded to a metrics crate or logs.

metrics.name: global_queue_depth
metrics.description: Tasks waiting in the global queue.

microservices_architecture.summary: Cross-service views come from distributed tracing, not from library metrics.
microservices_architecture.reason_none: End-to-end and service dependency views are produced by tracing (OneAgent PurePath or OpenTelemetry), which is covered by the language and framework modules.

event_driven_messaging.summary: Broker client libraries that expose their own metrics.

libraries.configuration: Micrometer binds RabbitMQ connection factory metrics when actuator and the AMQP starter are present; listener observation needs spring.rabbitmq.listener.simple.observation-enabled.

spring_boot_kafka.summary: Kafka client metrics (consumer lag, commit latency, records per poll) and Spring for Apache Kafka observations. These are not OneAgent defaults.

libraries.configuration: The Kafka consumer and producer maintain metrics internally; Spring Boot binds them to Micrometer (KafkaClientMetrics) when Actuator is present, and they are always readable over JMX.
libraries.export: Micrometer registry (names prefixed kafka.consumer.* and kafka.producer.*) or JMX.

metrics.name: records-lag-max
metrics.description: Maximum record lag across the consumer's partitions (micrometer kafka.consumer.fetch.manager.records.lag.max).

metrics.name: records-per-request-avg
metrics.description: Average records per fetch request (records consumed per poll).

metrics.name: assigned-partitions
metrics.description: Partitions currently assigned to the consumer.

metrics.name: record-send-rate
metrics.description: Records sent per second by the producer.

libraries.configuration: Set spring.kafka.listener.observation-enabled and spring.kafka.template.observation-enabled to record listener and template timers.
libraries.export: Through the Micrometer registry and tracing bridge.

metrics.name: spring.kafka.listener
metrics.description: Time spent in each Kafka listener invocation.

oauth2_identity.summary: Spring Security observations and client libraries.

libraries.configuration: Observations for filter chains, authentication and authorisation are recorded through the Micrometer observation registry in Spring Security 6 and later.

metrics.name: spring.security.filterchains
metrics.description: Time in the security filter chain.

jwt_authentication.summary: JWT libraries do not emit metrics.
jwt_authentication.reason_none: JWT parsing and verification libraries (jjwt, nimbus-jose-jwt, PyJWT, jsonwebtoken) emit no metrics; rejected-token counts must be added as custom instrumentation.

zero_trust.summary: Enforcement happens in the network or mesh layer.
zero_trust.reason_none: mTLS and policy decisions are produced by proxies and policy engines, not by application libraries.

source_github.reason_none: Source control and workflow telemetry come from the platform, not from application libraries.

cicd_harness.reason_none: Pipeline telemetry comes from the CI/CD platform.

cicd_ucd.reason_none: Deployment process telemetry comes from the deployment platform.

iac_terraform.reason_none: Infrastructure code emits no application metrics.

docker.summary: Container runtime metrics come from the runtime and platform.
docker.reason_none: Image and container resource metrics are produced by the container runtime and orchestrator, not application libraries.

kubernetes.summary: Cluster metrics come from platform exporters.
kubernetes.reason_none: Cluster and workload metrics come from kubelet, kube-state-metrics and the observability platform's Kubernetes integration, not from libraries inside the application.

gke.summary: Cluster metrics come from Google Cloud and the platform.
gke.reason_none: GKE cluster and node metrics are produced by Google Cloud Monitoring and managed Prometheus, not by application libraries.

openshift.summary: Cluster metrics come from the OpenShift monitoring stack.
openshift.reason_none: Platform metrics are produced by the cluster monitoring stack, not by application libraries.

rest_apis.summary: HTTP server and client metrics are emitted by the framework instrumentation.
rest_apis.reason_none: Request rate, latency and status metrics come from the web framework's instrumentation (for example Micrometer http.server.requests) and are listed under the framework modules.

api_gateway.summary: Gateway libraries that emit their own metrics.

libraries.configuration: Set spring.cloud.gateway.metrics.enabled=true with Actuator and a Micrometer registry.

metrics.name: spring.cloud.gateway.requests
metrics.description: Gateway request duration by route, outcome and status.

service_mesh.summary: Proxy metrics come from the mesh, not application libraries.
service_mesh.reason_none: Retry, timeout and mTLS counters are emitted by the sidecar proxy and control plane.

data_relational.summary: Connection pool libraries expose the saturation metrics that OneAgent does not capture.

libraries.library: JDBC connection pool metrics (HikariCP, DBCP, c3p0, UCP)
libraries.configuration: HikariCP publishes to Micrometer or Prometheus when a metrics tracker is set; other pools expose JMX MBeans.

data_postgres.summary: The PostgreSQL JDBC and native drivers emit no metrics.
data_postgres.reason_none: Driver libraries (pgjdbc, psycopg, pgx) emit no metrics; pool metrics are under the relational module and engine metrics come from exporters or platform extensions.

data_oracle.summary: Oracle UCP exposes pool statistics through JMX.

libraries.configuration: Enable UCP MBeans (setJMXEnabled) to expose pool statistics over JMX.
libraries.export: JMX (bridge to Micrometer or Prometheus with a JMX exporter).

data_sqlserver.summary: SQL Server drivers emit no metrics.
data_sqlserver.reason_none: The Microsoft JDBC, ADO.NET and ODBC drivers emit no metrics; pool metrics are under the relational module and engine metrics come from platform extensions.

data_bigquery.summary: BigQuery client libraries emit no metrics of their own.
data_bigquery.reason_none: Google Cloud client libraries offer optional OpenTelemetry tracing but no standard metric set; job and slot metrics come from the Google Cloud integration.

data_gcp_managed.summary: Connectors emit no metrics; managed database metrics come from Google Cloud.
data_gcp_managed.reason_none: The Cloud SQL connectors and proxy log connection events but do not publish application metrics; instance metrics come from Google Cloud monitoring.

caching.summary: Cache libraries expose hit ratio, size and eviction statistics when statistics are enabled.

libraries.configuration: Statistics are off by default; enable recordStats() (Spring Boot spring.cache.caffeine.spec=recordStats) and register the cache with Micrometer's CaffeineCacheMetrics.
MicrometerCommandLatencyRecorder is registered with the client resources (Spring Boot configures it when Micrometer is present).

metrics.name: lettuce.command.completion
metrics.description: Time from command dispatch to completion.

observability_dynatrace.summary: Export paths that carry application metrics into Dynatrace (they emit nothing themselves).

libraries.library: Micrometer Dynatrace registry and OpenTelemetry OTLP export to Dynatrace
libraries.configuration: Add the Dynatrace registry (or an OTLP exporter pointed at the tenant) and configure the endpoint and token through the secrets mechanism.
libraries.export: Dynatrace metric ingest API or OTLP endpoint.
